chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام ruled concerning the thief: when he steals, his right hand is cut off; if he steals another time, his left foot is cut off; then if he steals yet another time, he imprisons him, and his right foot is left for him to walk on to the place of relief, and his left hand with which he eats and cleanses himself. And he said: “Indeed, I feel shame before Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to leave him unable to benefit from anything, but rather I imprison him until he dies in prison.”
And he said: “The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم did not cut anything from a thief after his hand and his foot.”

key_terms.أَسْتَحْيِي: I feel shame, expressing reverence before Allah in limiting punishment
key_terms.السَّارِقِ: the thief, the one subject to the legal ruling for theft
key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, whose practice is cited as precedent
key_terms.رِجْلُهُ الْيُسْرَى: his left foot, the limb cut upon repeated theft
key_terms.سَجَنَهُ: he imprisoned him, the punishment after further repetition
key_terms.قُطِعَتْ: was cut off, referring to the prescribed bodily punishment
key_terms.يَمِينُهُ: his right hand, the limb first cut for theft

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling in Shi'i hadith on repeated theft after the first and second amputation?
ai.summary: This hadith reports the legal ruling of Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام regarding repeated theft, outlining escalating punishments and then imprisonment after the prescribed bodily penalties. It also attributes this limit to the practice of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, showing that further mutilation was not carried out beyond the hand and foot.
